Subject: High 5xx and blocked requests on dedicated pool (AuroraPay)

Karthik / David / Marissa,

We're seeing a large wave of blocked requests and 5xx errors from our Redwood Dedicated deployment starting ~08:12 PDT. Latency has spiked (p95 ~1.8s -> 6.2s) and the token queue depth is increasing; our metrics show our reserved throughput is being throttled and requests are timing out.

Attached: short log excerpt and a timestamped metric snapshot. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a capacity saturation in the dedicated GPU pool or a serving-layer regression? This behavior is impacting our production payments edge (about 15% of requests failing—transaction retries are compounding load).

Urgent—this is customer-impacting every minute.

Thanks,

Samir Rao
SRE, AuroraPay
ops@aurorapay.com

Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-19T08:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx and blocked requests on dedicated pool (AuroraPay)

Samir—thanks for the heads-up and logs.

Short status from our side:
- We see spike in queue depth on your reserved slots starting 08:11:40.
- Autoscaling hasn't kicked in because your plan is a strict reserved capacity contract; burst capacity is limited.
- There's a backend model variant that is heavier at longer sequences; it's getting routed for ~27% of traffic now.

Immediate asks / mitigations we're enacting now:
1) We're initiating an emergency routing change to send 35% of traffic to the fallback light quantized model which reduces per-token GPU cycles. ETA 6m.
2) David/Infra will open a burst window request to enable temporary overflow to shared-hosted capacity while we stabilize.
3) Irene (engineers) will triage recent kernel selection logs to ensure no regression.

Can you share the top call patterns (avg seq length, batch size) for the 08:10–08:25 window? Also let me know whether you prefer us to fail fast for long sequences to preserve tail latency.

I'll escalate to execs immediately for burst authorization.

-Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec visibility needed — AuroraPay reserved shortfall causing blocked request wave

Team—putting this on your radar and requesting immediate decision on burst authorization.

Summary:
- Customer: AuroraPay (priority, enterprise, contract AU-2026-09)
- Impact: 15% failed requests; elevated latency; payments edge trending to retry storms.
- Cause: Dedicated reserved pool for AuroraPay saturated; routing exposing heavier model variant; autoscale prevented by reserved-only policy.

Proposed ask to approve now:
A) Short-term: approve single 2-hour burst to Redwood Hosted to offload ~40% of peak QPS. This requires C-level signoff for credit and ops-runbook activation.
B) Mid-term: allow customer a temporary increase to reserved throughput while we optimize kernel selection / route to a quantized variant.

Potential risks/cost: expected hosted overage ~ $9–12k for 2 hours. Notable customer SLA exposure if we do nothing.

Action items assigned:
- David: open burst window + confirm capacity and routing change execution.
- Irene: finish triage on kernel/logs and confirm mitigation impact on latency within 20 minutes.
- Marissa: please coordinate an exec bridge with CS + AuroraPay leadership if we need credit approval.

I'll keep AuroraPay updated. If you approve, reply-all with "APPROVE BURST" and David will take it.

-Karthik
